title: Strict direct-image reduction and its completion-unit normalization
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subset A$ a finitely generated ideal, $A/I$ additive torsion, and $P_n=A/I^n$ finite as a set and perfect over $A$ for every $n\geq1$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum]. Let $u:U\to V$ be any morphism of schemes. For $T=U,V$ use the small pro-etale site, constant coefficient sheaves, and the unbounded derived category $D(T,A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathcal T_T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$, with constant-tower functor $\Delta_T$, and use its ringed diagram-site realization [def-weil-inverse-system, lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Put $\mathcal L_T=R\lim$, $\mathcal R_T(F)=\Delta_TF\otimes^L_{\Delta_T\underline A_T}(\underline{P_n}_T)_n$, and $C_T=\mathcal L_T\mathcal R_T$, with the specified completion unit $\eta$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit, lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]. Thus an object is complete when its completion unit is invertible. Write $i_{T,F}:\Delta_TF\to\mathcal R_TF$ for tensoring $\Delta_TF$ with the quotient augmentation $\Delta_T\underline A_T\to(\underline{P_n}_T)_n$; under $\mathcal L_T\Delta_TF\cong F$, one has $\mathcal L_T(i_{T,F})=\eta_F$.

Use canonical derived direct image $P=Ru_*$ and total derived termwise direct image $Q=R_u^{\mathcal T}$. Let $\chi_{u,F}:\Delta_V(PF)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\Delta_UF$ be the constant-tower comparison [lem-sf-cbc-constant-tower-direct-image-normalization]. Define $h_{u,F}:\mathcal R_V(PF)\to Q\mathcal R_UF$ by the diagram-site projection morphism adjoint to counit tensored with identity, for $\Delta_UF$ and $(\underline{P_n}_V)_n$, identifying its source through $\chi_{u,F}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Let $b_{u,N}:P\mathcal L_UN\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_VQN$ be the underived-composite normalized direct-image/derived-limit comparison, commuting with all tower projections [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison], and put
$$\rho_{u,F}=b_{u,\mathcal R_UF}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_V(h_{u,F}):C_V(PF)\longrightarrow P(C_UF).$$
For every $F\in D(U,A)$ this is a natural transformation satisfying the equality
$$\rho_{u,F}\circ\eta_{PF}=P(\eta_F).$$
For complete $K$, $h_{u,K}$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal T_V)$, natural in $K$, and its $n$-th evaluation is the canonical perfect-$P_n$ projection-formula isomorphism. In particular, as equality of the specified derived morphisms,
$$\mathcal L_V(h_{u,K})\circ\eta_{PK}=b_{u,\mathcal R_UK}\circ P(\eta_K).$$
All equalities are before any evaluation of derived tower morphisms; no uniform cohomological or Tor bounds are imposed.

proof.text:
Put $B_T=(\underline{P_n}_T)_n$. On the diagram sites the projection morphism is natural in both the source object and the coefficient object by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Its value at $\Delta_UF$, followed on the source by the natural constant-tower comparison $\chi_{u,F}\otimes1$, is exactly the specified $h_{u,F}$; consequently $h$ is natural in $F$. Clause (4) of [lem-sf-cbc-constant-tower-direct-image-normalization], with $f=u$ and $M=F$, applies to precisely these constant coefficient sheaves, quotient augmentation and counit-defined diagram projection. It gives, in $D(\mathcal T_V)$,
$$h_{u,F}i_{V,PF}=Q(i_{U,F})\chi_{u,F}.$$
This is an equality of strict derived-tower morphisms, valid for arbitrary $F$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-cbc-normalized-augmentation-transport] with $\mathcal D_T=D(T,A)$, $\mathcal E_T=D(\mathcal T_T)$, $B_T=\mathcal R_T$, $L_T=\mathcal L_T$, and the statement's $P,Q,i,\chi,b,h$. The $j_T$ are the stipulated constant-tower limit identifications. Step 1 supplies the augmentation square and naturality of $h$. The normalized constant comparison, clause (3) of [lem-sf-cbc-constant-tower-direct-image-normalization], gives $b_{\Delta_UF}=\mathcal L_V(\chi_F)$ under these identifications; naturality and invertibility of $b$ are supplied by [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. Thus all hypotheses of the transport lemma hold. Its $\eta$ and $\rho$ are exactly the specified ones here. Its two unit equations and naturality formula give the asserted equations for every $F$ and naturality of $\rho$, before evaluation.

proof.text: Compare the constant quotient presentation with the continuous-function presentation of the existing original-site strict reduction model [def-sp-constant-reduction-models]. At level n the canonical constant-to-function ring isomorphism intertwines the quotient maps. Balanced scalar-extension maps on pure tensors give inverse natural comparisons of the ordinary reduction levels. Quotient naturality makes them a strict tower isomorphism. Derive it using the universal reduction counits. The pure tensor formulas also prove compatibility with ordinary pullback. On adapted K-flat representatives, cancel the reduction counits and use both normalization equations to deduce compatibility with the derived pullback squares; resolving extensionality makes this a natural-transformation equality. Naturality of adjunction mates then conjugates the specified projection by these derived model isomorphisms. The original-site strict projection is invertible by [lem-sp-completion-mate-comparison], whose proof evaluates it, applies [lem-sp-constant-perfect-quotient-projection], and detects invertibility through levelwise cohomology. Thus the specified strict projection here is invertible for every ambient input. Mathlib mateEquiv_vcomp identifies its finite evaluation followed by evalR with finiteProjection. Since evalR is invertible, finiteProjection is invertible as well. Restrict to complete K and use Step 2 for the final equation. No uniform bound or compatible choice of perfect representatives is introduced.

lean.statement: theorem directImageReductionUnit (d : CompleteCoefficientDatum A) (_hfinite : ∀ n : ℕ, Finite (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (n + 1))) {U V : Scheme.{u}} (f : U ⟶ V) : (∀ F : DerivedCategory (Modules A U), (unit d.ideal V).app ((push A f).obj F) ≫ (comparison d.ideal f).app F = (push A f).map ((unit d.ideal U).app F)) ∧ (∀ (F F' : DerivedCategory (Modules A U)) (t : F ⟶ F'), (completion d.ideal V).map ((push A f).map t) ≫ (comparison d.ideal f).app F' = (comparison d.ideal f).app F ≫ (push A f).map ((completion d.ideal U).map t)) ∧ (∀ (F F' : DerivedCategory (Modules A U)) (t : F ⟶ F'), (reduction d.ideal V).map ((push A f).map t) ≫ (projection d.ideal f).app F' = (projection d.ideal f).app F ≫ (R A f).map ((reduction d.ideal U).map t)) ∧ (∀ K : DerivedCategory (Modules A U), IsIso ((unit d.ideal U).app K) → IsIso ((projection d.ideal f).app K) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, (ev A V n).map ((projection d.ideal f).app K) ≫ (evalR A f n).app ((reduction d.ideal U).obj K) = (finiteProjection d.ideal f n).app K) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, IsIso ((finiteProjection d.ideal f n).app K)) ∧ (unit d.ideal V).app ((push A f).obj K) ≫ (L A V).map ((projection d.ideal f).app K) = (push A f).map ((unit d.ideal U).app K) ≫ (limitPush A f).hom.app ((reduction d.ideal U).obj K))
